recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Engineer Who Went Looking For The Source Code", "body": "Chari trained as an engineer, with bachelor's and master's degrees, in a family where the options were engineer, doctor, or attorney, while his sister became a medical doctor and together they founded the Chari Center of Health in 1999. He says he set an intention to find a way for his engineering skills to help people heal, and two weeks later friends told him about a Santa Monica talk on how the voice reveals subconscious patterns. He learned the method, and reports the first person he ever worked on was himself."}, {"title": "The Bullying Pattern He Kept Recreating", "body": "He describes hiding in the library until dark to avoid bullies, then watching the same dynamic follow him into high school as status and class, into engineering school where professors told him he should be an actor, and into jobs, friendships, and relationships he fled by moving hundreds or thousands of miles. The faces and personalities changed, he says, but the energy was identical, until he reached the realization that the only common element in every situation was himself. Clearing that pattern, he reports, brought nurturing and supportive people he had no prior concept of."}, {"title": "Four Phases Of Programming, From Conception Onward", "body": "Chari lays out a model with four phases: conception, where he says a percentage of each parent's and each grandparent's unresolved emotions transfers into the forming child; nine months in the womb, absorbing the mother's arguments and frustrations; birth and the direct interface with parents; and finally the years to thirteen or fourteen, when whatever is said goes in without evaluation. Garton adds his biofield tuning experience of reading cesarean births and guilt patterns off the energy field, and pushes back with a soul choice caveat so expectant parents do not carry extra fear."}, {"title": "Missing Notes, Squashed Emotions, And Sympathetic Resonance", "body": "Rather than working from what a client tells him, Chari says he listens to the sound spectrum of the voice itself, hunting for the deficient note among the twelve that repeat across a piano's hundreds of keys. A note he can barely hear or cannot hear at all signals, in his account, an emotion squashing that key: anger, grief, self sabotage, worry, low self worth. His fix borrows sympathetic resonance, the way striking A on one piano vibrates the same string on an untouched second piano, to bring the missing note back up."}, {"title": "Humming Your Way Back Into Tune", "body": "The baseline program, Chari explains, is homework by email: music written in the key of the note that went quiet, roughly ten minutes of humming or singing along with a free phone tuner app confirming the pitch, then twenty minute tracks playing in the background. The tuner is the feedback half of biofeedback. He reports personality shifts, clients finally being heard at work, and follow up sessions a week or two later where the note has returned. Maintenance runs about monthly, he says, comparing it to oil changes and belt levels rather than a one time fix."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Deepak Chari of the Chari Institute joins InnerVerse to discuss his life's work engineering biofeedback technology that helps people achieve energetic balance and deprogram unhelpful subconscious loops. In this episode, Deepak describes how his method derived from healing his own negative patterns, the way conditioned adaptations implant in the deep mind through phases of life, how specific frequency can be applied to help with unique individual deficiencies, the universal law of sympathetic resonance, and much more.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we explore some of Deepak's favorite success stories with his modality, how this technique applies to the human biofield anatomy, the energetic dynamics of the throat chakra, deconstructing the western cult of positive thinking, proper processing of negative emotions, turning around addictive and suicidal tendencies, and how one person's choice to be whole ripples out to the entire world.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Entanglement and the Mirror of the Outer World", "body": "Deepak opens the extension with quantum physics, citing the observer effect and entanglement and recalling a line he attributes to Einstein, that it is hard to comprehend but impossible to deny. He then shares accounts from his practice in which relatives changed their behavior after sessions they knew nothing about, which he credits to the quantum field. Chance reads this as inner frustration being externalized, adds that our own patterns become invisible by proximity, like the nose on your face, and offers a rule of thumb for solo shadow work: whatever feels most done to you is probably how you are treating yourself."}, {"title": "The Sacral Chakra and What Is Hard to Digest", "body": "Hearing how one man's standing in his family turned around, Chance guesses from the anecdote alone that digestive trouble came with the pattern, and Deepak confirms it was a detail he had left out. Chance maps the sacral chakra as an axis with guilt and shame on the right and frustration, resentment and disappointment on the left, saying that when those expressions return to the middle they circulate as fulfillment, self-esteem, abundance and contentment. Deepak adds his view that the body takes language literally, recalling how he reframed what the client found hard to accept as hard to digest. Both enjoy finding two modalities speaking one language."}, {"title": "The Throat Chakra and the Voice as Truth", "body": "Chance describes the throat chakra as more than clear and courageous speech, tying it to being impeccable with your word, and asks whether the tone of a public figure's voice should inform whom we trust. Deepak declines to comment on any individual, saying fifteen years of work have convinced him the voice is the most accurate reflection of a person. He describes a throat pattern he calls emotional shutdown, formed when a child is squashed every time they speak, and says performers can still lose notes after an upset that no diaphragm technique reaches. He now senses the emotion first and lets the graphs provide a double confirmation."}, {"title": "Deconstructing the Cult of Positive Thinking", "body": "Chance, who has not studied The Secret directly, questions the habit of ignoring the negative, arguing that fear of how we are perceived pushes legitimate emotions into repression and that sadness belongs to the joy spectrum. Deepak pictures a bullied child told to just think positive, who concludes their problems do not matter, and urges people to vocalize what bothers them before the pressure explodes. Chance offers a clue to hidden repression, your sensitivity to that emotion in others, and says accepting it in them is your own protection. Deepak, a self-described fixer, says he had to learn to just listen, which Chance calls the wellness in the witness."}, {"title": "Choice, Ripple Effects, and a Global Mission", "body": "Asked what he rarely gets to discuss, Deepak says his work began as a way to clear his own bullying pattern and grew far beyond it, because each person he helps is connected to dozens more, and some clients who arrived in crisis went on to start foundations for others. He explains that he only takes clients who can still feel their emotions and who want the change themselves. Chance calls that choice the free will underpinning of the universe. Deepak names his hidden mission as shifting global consciousness through a small percentage of people, and Chance, citing Jung, frames the outer world as the outermost layer of the psyche."}]
